title: Does Claude know which comments are due?
text: Someone assumes Claude knows which comment deadlines are coming due on its own. It doesn't, it only tracks what a skill tells it to track. The real question, how does Claude track a filing deadline? A federal agency proposes a rule and

title: No built-in connection to any docket
text: Opens a public comment period often just 60 days before it can finalize. Miss that window and your objection never reaches the record. The easy assumption is that Claude is already watching that window the way a person might watch a calendar, but Claude has no built-in connection to any docket. What it is is a skill, a folder of instructions called comments. The skill MD inside that

title: A skill is three instructions — the anchor
text: Folder says three things, review open comment periods, log decisions, track deadlines. Claude reads that file fresh each time, it keeps no memory of a docket from any other session. Watch one rule, a proposal opens its comment window on March 2nd, 60 days to respond. The skill logs that date the moment it's told and starts the clock. When day 60

title: Logged on time — and only that
text: Arrives, the skill doesn't file anything itself, a person still decides and records that call with one flag, filed, not filed, or waived. For March 2nd's rule, the log shows filed on day 59, but a decision logged on time doesn't mean the comment itself was any good, the skill only kept the date. And a rule with no logged decision isn't necessarily missed, it might be tracked somewhere the skill never saw. A skill

title: Carry-out
text: Like this doesn't know the law and it doesn't decide anything, it only remembers the date you gave it. Filed, waived, or missed, that call is still yours to make. Your turn, here's the

title: Your turn
text: Prompt, read it with me. Paste in a proposed rule with its comment deadline, then ask log this with the deadline and ask me before the deadline which way I want it recorded, filed, not filed, or waived. Don't decide for me. Liam in forbear.
